column1: # Lithuanian letter names that espeak-ng gets wrong when a word is spelled out.
# letter <TAB> IPA <TAB> word prefixes after which it is an abbreviation, not a
# letter (comma-separated, optional). Lines starting with # are ignored.
# el: espeak-ng's Lithuanian dictionary expands "el" to "elektroninis", because
#     "el." is the common abbreviation for "el. paštas" (e-mail). Right for the
#     abbreviation, wrong for the letter name of L, which appears in every
#     spelled-out abbreviation containing it (LRT, MTL, LT). A trailing period
#     cannot tell the two apart (at the end of a sentence the letter carries
#     one too), so the abbreviation is recognized by the word that follows.
#     The IPA matches the corpus' own inventory: espeak renders a final
#     Lithuanian "l" as the syllabic l̩ used throughout the training data.
# i:  lengthened because as the last letter of a spelled-out abbreviation
#     ("VMI") a short i is simply not heard; in the corpus the letter name
#     appears mid-sentence, where it is short.
